systeme:
Tu rédiges les articles développés d'un journal personnel imprimé, en français, à partir d'un article source complet (souvent en anglais).

Objectif : que le lecteur comprenne le sujet, ses tenants et ses aboutissants, sans lire l'article d'origine.

Règles impératives :
- Fidélité absolue à l'article : n'ajoute AUCUNE information extérieure, ne prête à personne une position qu'il n'a pas exprimée, conserve exactement les chiffres, les noms et les affiliations.
- Longueur : le total des caractères (chapô + intertitres + paragraphes + synthèse) ne doit PAS dépasser la limite indiquée. Vise 90 à 100 % de cette limite, jamais moins de 90 % : la mise en page réserve exactement cette place et un encadré à moitié vide est un défaut. Pour y parvenir, développe les faits, chiffres, acteurs et contexte présents dans l'article (sans rien inventer).
- Format indiqué dans la demande :
  • « long » (demi-page) : 3 à 5 sections, synthèse de 2 phrases ;
  • « court » (quart de page) : 1 ou 2 sections qui donnent les informations clés (faits, chiffres, acteurs, enjeu), puis une synthèse d'une ou deux phrases au maximum.
- Structure :
  • « titre » : titre français informatif, 80 caractères maximum.
  • « chapo » : une phrase qui pose le sujet, 200 caractères maximum.
  • « sections » : selon le format, chacune avec un « intertitre » court et un « texte » d'un paragraphe. Adapte les intertitres au type d'article, par exemple :
      débat ou controverse : Le déclencheur · De quoi parle-t-on · Les arguments pour · Les risques · Les contre-arguments
      annonce ou fait d'actualité : Ce qui est annoncé · Le contexte · Ce que ça change · Les limites
      étude ou recherche : La question · La méthode · Les résultats · Les réserves
      méthode d'entraînement : Le principe · Ce que dit la science · Comment l'appliquer · Les précautions
      réglementation : Ce qui change · Qui est concerné · Le calendrier · Les points de vigilance
  • « synthese » : 2 phrases (format long) ou 1 à 2 phrases (format court) qui résument l'ensemble.
- Style : français soigné, clair, sans tournures calquées sur l'anglais, sans emphase.
- « republication » : si l'article indique qu'il a été publié initialement à une date antérieure (republication), indique « paru initialement en <mois année> » ; sinon chaîne vide.

Réponds uniquement en JSON, selon cette structure :
{"titre": "…", "chapo": "…", "sections": [{"intertitre": "…", "texte": "…"}], "synthese": "…", "republication": ""}
contenu:
Vérification des sources complémentaires : avant de rédiger, vérifie que chaque SOURCE numérotée à partir de 2 traite bien du MÊME fait que la SOURCE 1 (même événement, mêmes acteurs). Ignore entièrement celles qui n'en traitent pas et donne leurs numéros dans « sources_ecartees ». Si, sans elles, la matière ne suffit pas pour un article fiable, réponds seulement {"insuffisant": true, "titre": "…", "texte": "…"} : une brève en français (titre de 90 caractères au plus, 2 à 3 phrases d'environ 450 caractères), uniquement d'après la SOURCE 1.
Format : long
Limite de longueur : 4500 caractères au total.
Édition numérique, lue sur téléphone, sans contrainte de page : la limite suit la matière disponible dans la source. Adapte le nombre de sections à la longueur : 2 sections sous 2 000 caractères, 3 ou 4 jusqu'à 3 500, 4 à 6 au-delà ; même règle de longueur (90 à 100 % de la limite). N'étire jamais une source mince : mieux vaut un article court et exact.
Le texte réunit plusieurs sources sur le même sujet (SOURCE 1, SOURCE 2…). Croise-les sans rien ajouter ; si elles divergent, dis-le en nommant la source.
Source : Al Jazeera
Rubrique : Monde
Date du flux : 20/11/2026
Auteur : Leena Fraihat; Leila Minkara
Titre d'origine : Iran war live: Houthis escalate attacks on Saudi capital

ARTICLE :
SOURCE 1 (Al Jazeera) :
Saudi-led coalition forces have intercepted multiple Houthi missiles, marking the second night the Gulf country is faced with fire after a tower in Riyadh’s financial centre was damaged yesterday.
The Houthi health ministry says attacks on Yemen’s capital, Sanaa, have killed 10 people over the past two days as the internationally recognised Yemeni government and the Saudi-led coalition trade fire with the Iran-backed rebel group.

  - The Saudi-led coalition says it has intercepted and destroyed two separate Houthi drones headed towards Saudi Arabia’s southern region.

These two alerts were the second and third of the day.

If a government funding bill does not cut off spending for his war, I will vote no. — Tammy Duckworth (@SenDuckworth) November 20, 2026
- 59m ago(02:15 GMT) Israeli strike on Gaza hospital kills doctor, friend of US Representative-elect Hamawy A newly-elected US representative has said a friend and fellow physician was killed by the Israeli air strike on one of Gaza’s largest hospitals last week. US Representative-elect Dr Adam Hamawy said his friend, Dr Rizk Abu Shaira, was killed in the attack on Nasser medical complex in southern Gaza. “I remember Dr. Shaira as a surgeon who worked day and night in impossible conditions to save as many lives as he could; as the carnage piled up”, Hamawy wrote in a post on X. “Come January, as a Member of Congress, I will work every day to win a full arms embargo on Israel,” said Hamawy, a New Jersey doctor whose first term in the House of Representatives will begin at the new year. The November 11 strike on the medical centre west of Khan Younis killed six Palestinians and wounded at least 20 more. Just over a week ago, Israel bombed the surgical wing of Nasser Hospital in Gaza. Lost to the latest horror in this genocide was my friend & colleague Dr. Rizk Abu Shaira. — Dr. Adam Hamawy (@HamawyForNJ) November 20, 2026
- 1h ago(02:01 GMT) Saudi-led coalition intercepts second drone in south The Saudi-led coalition says it has intercepted and destroyed a second drone launched by Houthi forces towards Saudi Arabia’s southern region. Again, the force’s spokesperson, Turki al-Maliki, made the announcement in a post on X.
- 1h ago(02:00 GMT) WATCH: Mosque torched in Israel sparks political backlash against Netanyahu
- 1h ago(01:45 GMT) Attack hit Riyadh skyscraper housing sovereign wealth fund, Saudi says The Houthi attack on Riyadh struck Saudi Arabia’s tallest building, which houses the country’s sovereign wealth fund, Saudi civil defence reported today. Images distributed by state media identified the building as the Public Investment Fund (PIF) tower, the headquarters of Saudi Arabia’s sovereign wealth fund and Riyadh’s tallest skyscraper. No one was injured in the attack, which struck the Saudi capital’s financial district. The agency said the attack damaged both the tower and nearby buildings. The Saudi-led coalition had said earlier that it intercepted missiles fired towards Riyadh and the south after a loud boom was heard in the capital. Read more here.
- 1h ago(01:30 GMT) Pentagon does not have overarching plan on munitions shortage, says US GAO The US Government Accountability Office (GAO) has said the Pentagon does not have an overarching plan to address its “persistent munitions shortages”. The Department of Defense (DOD) has also not “designated an office or entity” to manage munition inventory improvement actions, the GAO said in a recommendations report. According to the GAO, the Pentagon has taken steps to address the shortage, including establishing working groups to identify ways to increase munition production. However, the US war in Iran has placed increased pressure on the Pentagon’s munitions inventory. “Without a plan, it’s harder for DOD to know whether its munitions production efforts are really addressing department-wide needs”, the GAO said.
- 1h ago(01:16 GMT) Saudi-led coalition intercepts drone in south The Saudi-led coalition says it has intercepted and destroyed a drone launched by Houthi forces towards Saudi Arabia’s southern region, spokesman Turki al-Maliki said in a post on X.
- 1h ago(01:15 GMT) White House national cyber director Cairncross steps down White House National Cyber Director Sean Cairncross has reportedly stepped down amid widespread outages that have hit US air travel, banking and national security systems over the past week. Cairncross, who advises President Donald Trump on cybersecurity policy and strategy, is leaving to give the White House time to replace him before Democrats take control of Congress in January, US news outlet Axios reported. Top US officials have said there is no evidence the outages are linked or were caused by cyberattacks or hostile foreign actors. A US National Security Agency system has remained down for a third day in a row, reportedly due to a technical issue during maintenance.
- 2h ago(01:00 GMT) Photos: Aden tightens security at checkpoints as Houthis advance
- 2h ago(00:45 GMT) Iranian attacks have damaged 26 US sites across Middle East: AP More than 115 strikes claimed by Iran or Iranian-aligned groups damaged 26 military bases and other sites with US assets through August, according to an analysis by The Associated Press (AP) news agency published on October 31. The analysis, which used satellite imagery, determined that Iran’s attacks on more than two dozen US bases in the Middle East focused on early-warning systems before hitting aircraft and buildings. It shows that Ali al-Salem airbase in Kuwait was struck at least 30 times after the United States and Israel launched the war in February. At least 15 aircraft hangars, numerous warehouses and 10 buildings near a residential area were damaged or destroyed on the base. Iran’s strikes caused billions of dollars’ worth of damage to US equipment, AP reported.
- 2h ago(00:40 GMT) Air strikes hit Yemen’s al-Shamaitain district
- 2h ago(00:30 GMT) Yemen asks Italy to add Houthis to ‘terrorism lists’ After meeting Italian Foreign Minister Antonio Tajani, Yemen’s foreign minister, Afrah al-Zouba, has called on Italy to designate Houthi forces as “a terrorist organisation”, as Yemen did on Monday. “I briefed him on Yemen’s law designating the Houthi militia as a terrorist organisation,” al-Zouba said in a post on X, “and called on Italy and our European partners to take a similar step by adding it to terrorism lists and cutting off its sources of funding.” She added that she appreciated “Italy’s steadfast support for the Yemeni government” and “its condemnation of the Houthi militia’s terrorist attacks”.
- 2h ago(00:16 GMT) Saudi Arabia lifts emergency warning for Jizan Saudi authorities say the danger has passed in the city of Jizan, shortly after issuing an emergency alert. The Saudi Civil Defense told citizens to continue to follow safety instructions and avoid gatherings.

We’re standing up to Trump with our new majority in January,” he said. Earlier, we reported that Senate Republicans rejected the resolution, which sought to direct US President Donald Trump to remove US forces from hostilities with Iran, in a 51-to-48 vote. Once again, Democrats voted to end this deadly, costly war of choice in Iran. Once again, Republicans blocked it. We will never back down on trying to end this war. No more waiting for Republicans to find their spine. We’re standing up to Trump with our new majority in January. — Mark Warner (@MarkWarner) November 19, 2026

The Saudi Civil Defense’s “potential danger” warning advised citizens to remain indoors or proceed to the safest nearby building.

  - A skyscraper in Riyadh’s financial centre has been damaged by a Houthi-claimed attack condemned by Qatar, Kuwait and the Gulf Cooperation Council.
  - Iran’s Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps Navy says two tankers have caught fire after hitting naval mines in the southern part of the Strait of Hormuz.
  - Yemeni government forces say they have targeted multiple Houthi sites south of the besieged city of Taiz.
  - Saudi Arabia has issued 10 emergency warnings across several regions as the Houthis continue to launch missiles towards the kingdom.
  - The Houthi Health Ministry says attacks on Yemen’s capital, Sanaa, have killed 10 people over the past two days.
  - Gaza’s Health Ministry says at least 300 children have died while waiting for Israeli permission to leave for life-saving medical treatment.
  - The US-Israel war on Iran has cost the United States more than $48bn, a Defense Department official has said.
